## Load in Data with fbi Package
```{r}
# Load in data from 1959-2025
qd <- fredqd(
  file = "./current.csv",
  date_start = as.Date("1959-12-01"),
  date_end   = as.Date("2025-12-01"),
  transform  = FALSE
)

# Keep variables mentioned in proposal
# date - quarter date of observation (YYYY-MM-DD)
# GDPC1 - Real Gross Domestic Product ($B)
# UNRATE - Civilian Unemployment Rate (%)
# CPIAUCSL - Consumer Price Index for all Urban Consumers (1982-1984=100)
# GS10 - 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate (%)
# TB3MS -  3-Month Treasury Bill Secondary Market Rate (%)
vars <- c("date", "GDPC1", "UNRATE", "CPIAUCSL", "INDPRO", "GS10", "TB3MS")
df <- qd[, vars]

# Rename variables after log transformations
df$gdp_growth <- c(NA, diff(log(df$GDPC1)))
df$inflation  <- c(NA, diff(log(df$CPIAUCSL)))
df$ip_growth  <- c(NA, diff(log(df$INDPRO)))

# Calculate treasury yield spread
df$spread     <-df$GS10 - df$TB3MS

# Calculate lag variables (values from previous quarter)
df$lag_gdp_growth <- c(NA, head(df$gdp_growth, -1))
df$lag_unrate     <- c(NA, head(df$UNRATE, -1))
df$lag_inflation  <- c(NA, head(df$inflation, -1))
df$lag_ip_growth  <- c(NA, head(df$ip_growth, -1))
df$lag_spread     <- c(NA, head(df$spread, -1))

df_final <- na.omit(df[, c(
  "date", "gdp_growth", "lag_gdp_growth", "lag_unrate",
  "lag_inflation", "lag_ip_growth", "lag_spread"
)])

# Inspect data
head(df_final)
summary(df_final)
nrow(df_final)
```

# 3.) Frequentist Model

## Fit OLS Model
```{r}
# Extract variable names
X_names <- colnames(df_final)
X_names <- X_names[3:ncol(df_final)]
formula <- as.formula(paste("gdp_growth ~", paste(X_names, collapse = " + ")))

# Scale data for regression
df_final_scaled <- as.data.frame(scale(df_final[,-1]))

# Use lm() to fit OLS model for gdp growth
freq_mod <- lm(formula, data=df_final_scaled)

# Summary of OLS model
summary(freq_mod)
```
## OLS Model Diagnostics

### Heteroskedasticity
```{r}
# Plot residuals
plot(freq_mod, which = 1)
```
```{r}
# Perform BP-Test on model
bptest(freq_mod)
```

### Normality of Residuals
```{r}
# Inspect normality of residuals
qqnorm(freq_mod$residuals, main = "QQ Plot of Residuals")
qqline(freq_mod$residuals)
```

```{r}
# Inspect normality of residuals with Shapiro-Wilk Test
shapiro.test(resid(freq_mod))
```
## Remarks
Residual diagnostics suggest mild deviations from normality, particularly in the tails, and evidence of heteroskedasticity. Given the nature of macroeconomic data, these findings are expected. To address potential heteroskedasticity, robust standard errors were employed in inference.

## Robust Standard Errors
```{r}
# Robust Standard Errors to deal with heteroskedasticity
coeftest(freq_mod, vcov = vcovHC(freq_mod, type = "HC1"))
```
## Probability of Negative GDP Growth
For this part, we want to compute:

$$
P(Y_t<0\:|\:X_t)
$$

Where $Y_t$ is GDP growth. We will do this with unscaled data.

Our model implies:

$$
Y_t\approx{}N(\hat{\mu}_t,\hat{\sigma}^2)
$$
Where $\hat{\mu}_t$ is the fitted regression value, and $\hat{\sigma}$ is the residual standard error.

From this, we have:

$$
P(Y_t<0)=\Phi{}\left( \frac{0-\hat{\mu}_t}{\hat{\sigma}} \right)
$$
Which we can use pnorm() to calculate.

```{r}
# Fit unscaled model
freq_mod_unscaled <- lm(formula, data = df_final)

# Make predictions with uncertainty
pred <- predict(freq_mod_unscaled, newdata = df_final, se.fit = TRUE)

# Store values to use for pnorm()
mu_hat <- pred$fit
se_mu <- pred$se.fit
sigma_hat <- sigma(freq_mod_unscaled)

# Calculate predictive SD for each observation
pred_sd <- sqrt(se_mu^2 + sigma_hat^2)

# Calculate probability of negative GDP growth
recession_prob <- pnorm(0, mean = mu_hat, sd = pred_sd)

# Attach results to df
df_final$pred_gdp_growth <- mu_hat
df_final$pred_sd <- pred_sd
df_final$recession_prob <- recession_prob

# Inspect results
head(df_final[, c("date", "gdp_growth", "pred_gdp_growth", "pred_sd", "recession_prob")])

# Plot probability over time
plot(df_final$date, df_final$recession_prob,
     type = "l",
     lwd = 2,
     main = "Frequentist Estimated Probability of Negative GDP Growth",
     xlab = "Quarter",
     ylab = "Probability")

# Add vertical lines for key quarters
abline(v = as.Date(c(
  "2001-03-01",
  "2002-03-01",
  "2007-03-01",
  "2009-03-01",
  "2020-03-01",
  "2021-03-01"
)), col = "blue", lty = 2)
```

```{r}
# Set seed for predictive checking
set.seed(123)

# Define constants
S <- 5000
N <- nrow(df_final)

# Calculate fitted values and standard error
mu_hat <- fitted(freq_mod_unscaled)
sigma_hat <- sigma(freq_mod_unscaled)

# Define storage matrix for predictions
y_rep_freq <- matrix(NA, nrow = N, ncol = S)

# Draw replications of our frequentist model
for (s in 1:S) {
  y_rep_freq[, s] <- rnorm(N, mean = mu_hat, sd = sigma_hat)
}
```

```{r}

legend("topright",

```

```{r}
# Use the same cutoff as your Bayesian PPC / t-model check
extreme_cutoff <- -0.02

# Observed count
obs_extreme_neg <- sum(df_final$gdp_growth < extreme_cutoff)

# Simulated counts from existing y_rep_freq matrix
sim_extreme_neg <- apply(y_rep_freq, 2, function(y) {
  sum(y < extreme_cutoff)
})

# Plot simulated counts vs observed count
hist(sim_extreme_neg,
     breaks = 30,
     main = "Frequentist Predictive Check: Extreme Negative GDP Quarters",
     xlab = paste("Number of quarters with GDP growth <", extreme_cutoff))

abline(v = obs_extreme_neg, col = "red", lwd = 2)

legend("topright",
       legend = paste("Observed =", obs_extreme_neg),
       col = "red",
       lwd = 2,
       bty = "n")

# Predictive p-value style comparison
freq_extreme_p <- mean(sim_extreme_neg >= obs_extreme_neg)

# Summary table
freq_extreme_table <- data.frame(
  Statistic = "Extreme negative GDP quarters",
  Cutoff = extreme_cutoff,
  Observed = obs_extreme_neg,
  Simulated_Mean = mean(sim_extreme_neg),
  Simulated_2.5 = quantile(sim_extreme_neg, 0.025),
  Simulated_97.5 = quantile(sim_extreme_neg, 0.975),
  Predictive_P_Value = freq_extreme_p
)

knitr::kable(freq_extreme_table,
             digits = 4,
             caption = "Frequentist predictive check for extreme negative GDP quarters")
```


# 4.) Bayesian Model
## Model Definition
We define our Bayesian model as such:

$$
y_t\sim{}N(\mu_t,\sigma)
$$

$$
\mu_t=\beta_0+\beta_1X_{t-1}
$$
We have weakly informative priors of:

$$
\beta_j\sim{}N(0,5)
$$
## JAGS on Unscaled Data

### JAGS Setup
```{r}
# Model String for Bayesian MLR
modelString <- "
model {
## sampling
for (i in 1:N) {
    mu[i] <- beta_0 +
             beta_gdp * lag_gdp[i] +
             beta_unrate * lag_unrate[i] +
             beta_inflation * lag_inflation[i] +
             beta_ip * lag_ip[i] +
             beta_spread * lag_spread[i]
             
  y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], tau)
}
  
## priors
beta_0          ~ dnorm(mu0, g0)
beta_gdp       ~ dnorm(mu1, g1)
beta_unrate    ~ dnorm(mu2, g2)
beta_inflation ~ dnorm(mu3, g3)
beta_ip        ~ dnorm(mu4, g4)
beta_spread    ~ dnorm(mu5, g5)
sigma ~ dt(mu_sigma, tau_sigma, nu_sigma) T(0, upper_sigma)
tau <- pow(sigma, -2)
}
"

# Pass data and hyperparameter values
y <- as.vector(df_final$gdp_growth)
lag_gdp <- as.vector(df_final$lag_gdp)
lag_unrate <- as.vector(df_final$lag_unrate)
lag_inflation <- as.vector(df_final$lag_inflation)
lag_ip <- as.vector(df_final$lag_ip)
lag_spread <- as.vector(df_final$lag_spread)

N <- length(y)

mu_sigma <- 0
nu_sigma <- 1
upper_sigma <- 1000000

the_data <- list(
  y = y,
  lag_gdp = lag_gdp,
  lag_unrate = lag_unrate,
  lag_inflation = lag_inflation,
  lag_ip = lag_ip,
  lag_spread = lag_spread,
  N = N,
  mu0 = 0, g0 = 1/25,
  mu1 = 0, g1 = 1/25,
  mu2 = 0, g2 = 1/25,
  mu3 = 0, g3 = 1/25,
  mu4 = 0, g4 = 1/25,
  mu5 = 0, g5 = 1/25,
  mu_sigma = 0,
  tau_sigma = 1/25,
  nu_sigma = 1,
  upper_sigma = 1e6
)

initsfunction <- function(chain){
  return(list(
    .RNG.seed = 100 + chain,
    .RNG.name = "base::Mersenne-Twister"
  ))
}

posterior_MLR <- run.jags(modelString,
                      n.chains = 3,
                      data = the_data,
                      monitor = c("beta_0", "beta_gdp", "beta_unrate",
                                  "beta_inflation", "beta_ip", "beta_spread",
                                  "sigma"),
                      adapt = 2000,
                      burnin = 10000,
                      sample = 10000,
                      thin = 50,
                      inits = initsfunction)
```
```{r}
# Print summary
summary(posterior_MLR)
```

## Jags on Scaled Data

### JAGS Setup
```{r}
# Model String for Bayesian MLR
modelStringScaled <- "
model {
## sampling
for (i in 1:N) {
    mu[i] <- beta_0 +
             beta_gdp * lag_gdp[i] +
             beta_unrate * lag_unrate[i] +
             beta_inflation * lag_inflation[i] +
             beta_ip * lag_ip[i] +
             beta_spread * lag_spread[i]
             
  y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], tau)
}
  
## priors
beta_0          ~ dnorm(mu0, g0)
beta_gdp       ~ dnorm(mu1, g1)
beta_unrate    ~ dnorm(mu2, g2)
beta_inflation ~ dnorm(mu3, g3)
beta_ip        ~ dnorm(mu4, g4)
beta_spread    ~ dnorm(mu5, g5)
sigma ~ dt(mu_sigma, tau_sigma, nu_sigma) T(0, upper_sigma)
tau <- pow(sigma, -2)
}
"

# Pass data and hyperparameter values
y <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$gdp_growth)
lag_gdp <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_gdp)
lag_unrate <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_unrate)
lag_inflation <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_inflation)
lag_ip <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_ip)
lag_spread <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_spread)

N <- length(y)

mu_sigma <- 0
nu_sigma <- 1
upper_sigma <- 1000000

the_data <- list(
  y = y,
  lag_gdp = lag_gdp,
  lag_unrate = lag_unrate,
  lag_inflation = lag_inflation,
  lag_ip = lag_ip,
  lag_spread = lag_spread,
  N = N,
  mu0 = 0, g0 = 1,
  mu1 = 0, g1 = 1,
  mu2 = 0, g2 = 1,
  mu3 = 0, g3 = 1,
  mu4 = 0, g4 = 1,
  mu5 = 0, g5 = 1,
  mu_sigma = 0,
  tau_sigma = 1,
  nu_sigma = 1,
  upper_sigma = 1e6
)

initsfunction <- function(chain){
  return(list(
    .RNG.seed = 100 + chain,
    .RNG.name = "base::Mersenne-Twister"
  ))
}

posterior_MLR_scaled <- run.jags(modelStringScaled,
                      n.chains = 3,
                      data = the_data,
                      monitor = c("beta_0", "beta_gdp", "beta_unrate",
                                  "beta_inflation", "beta_ip", "beta_spread",
                                  "sigma"),
                      adapt = 2000,
                      burnin = 10000,
                      sample = 10000,
                      thin = 10,
                      inits = initsfunction)
```

### Interpretation and inference

For both of our JAGS simulations, each of our monitored parameters seemingly converges to a stable distribution.

## Probability of Negative GDP Growth (with unscaled data)

```{r}
# Convert posterior results to matrix
post <- as.matrix(as.mcmc(posterior_MLR))

# Extract predictor values from data
X <- model.matrix(~ lag_gdp_growth + lag_unrate + lag_inflation +
                    lag_ip_growth + lag_spread, data = df_final)

# Create vector of coeffecient draws
beta_draws <- cbind(post[, "beta_0"],
                    post[, "beta_gdp"],
                    post[, "beta_unrate"],
                    post[, "beta_inflation"],
                    post[, "beta_ip"],
                    post[, "beta_spread"])

# Calculate mu response
mu_post <- beta_draws %*% t(X)

# Create posterior sigma draws vector
sigma_post <- post[, "sigma"]

# Calculate probability of negative GDP growth
bayes_prob_neg <- sapply(1:ncol(mu_post), function(j) {
  mean(pnorm(0, mean = mu_post[, j], sd = sigma_post))
})

# Store results in dataframe
df_final$bayes_prob_neg <- bayes_prob_neg
```

```{r}
# Plot probability over time
plot(df_final$date, df_final$bayes_prob_neg, type="l", lwd=2,
     main="Bayesian Posterior Probability of Negative GDP Growth",
     xlab="Quarter", ylab="Probability")

# Add vertical lines for key quarters
abline(v = as.Date(c(
  "2001-03-01",
  "2002-03-01",
  "2007-03-01",
  "2009-03-01",
  "2020-03-01",
  "2021-03-01"
)), col = "blue", lty = 2)
```


# 5.) Full Model Comparison

## Coefficient Estimates
```{r}
# Obtain frequentist robust results from scaled model
robust_vcov <- vcovHC(freq_mod, type = "HC1")
robust_test <- coeftest(freq_mod, vcov = robust_vcov)

# Extract estimates, se, p-values, and interval bounds
freq_est <- robust_test[, "Estimate"]
freq_se  <- robust_test[, "Std. Error"]
freq_p   <- robust_test[, "Pr(>|t|)"]
freq_lower <- freq_est - 1.96 * freq_se
freq_upper <- freq_est + 1.96 * freq_se

# Convert Bayesian posterior draws to matrix
post_scaled <- as.matrix(as.mcmc(posterior_MLR_scaled))

# Define vector of param names
bayes_params <- c("beta_0", "beta_gdp", "beta_unrate",
                  "beta_inflation", "beta_ip", "beta_spread")

# Calculate mean, lower, and upper bounds from Bayesian Posterior draws
bayes_mean  <- apply(post_scaled[, bayes_params], 2, mean)
bayes_lower <- apply(post_scaled[, bayes_params], 2, quantile, probs = 0.025)
bayes_upper <- apply(post_scaled[, bayes_params], 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)

# Construct table comparing frequentist and Bayesian results
comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("(Intercept)", "lag_gdp_growth", "lag_unrate",
               "lag_inflation", "lag_ip_growth", "lag_spread"),
  Freq_Estimate = as.numeric(freq_est),
  Freq_Robust_SE = as.numeric(freq_se),
  Freq_95CI_Lower = as.numeric(freq_lower),
  Freq_95CI_Upper = as.numeric(freq_upper),
  Freq_pvalue = as.numeric(freq_p),
  Bayes_Mean = c(bayes_mean["beta_0"],
                 bayes_mean["beta_gdp"],
                 bayes_mean["beta_unrate"],
                 bayes_mean["beta_inflation"],
                 bayes_mean["beta_ip"],
                 bayes_mean["beta_spread"]),
  Bayes_95CrI_Lower = c(bayes_lower["beta_0"],
                        bayes_lower["beta_gdp"],
                        bayes_lower["beta_unrate"],
                        bayes_lower["beta_inflation"],
                        bayes_lower["beta_ip"],
                        bayes_lower["beta_spread"]),
  Bayes_95CrI_Upper = c(bayes_upper["beta_0"],
                        bayes_upper["beta_gdp"],
                        bayes_upper["beta_unrate"],
                        bayes_upper["beta_inflation"],
                        bayes_upper["beta_ip"],
                        bayes_upper["beta_spread"])
)

# Display table
knitr::kable(comparison_table,
             digits = 4,
             caption = "Frequentist and Bayesian coefficient comparison (scaled data)")
```

```{r}
       col = "gray60", lty = 3)

       bty = "n")
```

## Predictive Fit
```{r}
# Compute frequentist fit metrics
freq_rmse <- sqrt(mean((df_final$gdp_growth - df_final$pred_gdp_growth)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
freq_mae  <- mean(abs(df_final$gdp_growth - df_final$pred_gdp_growth), na.rm = TRUE)

# Compute Bayesian posterior mean fitted values
post_unscaled <- as.matrix(as.mcmc(posterior_MLR))

# Extract unscaled predictor variables
X_unscaled <- model.matrix(~ lag_gdp_growth + lag_unrate + lag_inflation +
                             lag_ip_growth + lag_spread,
                           data = df_final)

# Put together unscaled draws
beta_draws_unscaled <- cbind(
  post_unscaled[, "beta_0"],
  post_unscaled[, "beta_gdp"],
  post_unscaled[, "beta_unrate"],
  post_unscaled[, "beta_inflation"],
  post_unscaled[, "beta_ip"],
  post_unscaled[, "beta_spread"]
)

# Compute mu and predicted means
mu_post_unscaled <- beta_draws_unscaled %*% t(X_unscaled)
bayes_pred_mean <- colMeans(mu_post_unscaled)

# Insert results into data
df_final$bayes_pred_gdp_growth <- bayes_pred_mean

# Calculate Bayesian fit metrics
bayes_rmse <- sqrt(mean((df_final$gdp_growth - df_final$bayes_pred_gdp_growth)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
bayes_mae  <- mean(abs(df_final$gdp_growth - df_final$bayes_pred_gdp_growth), na.rm = TRUE)

# Create comparison table for metrics
fit_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Frequentist", "Bayesian"),
  RMSE = c(freq_rmse, bayes_rmse),
  MAE  = c(freq_mae, bayes_mae)
)

# Display table
knitr::kable(fit_comparison,
             digits = 5,
             caption = "Predictive fit comparison on unscaled GDP growth")
```

# 6.) Other Bayesian Models

## t-distributed error model
```{r}
# Model string for t distributed errors
modelString_t <- "
model {

  for (i in 1:N) {
    mu[i] <- beta_0 +
             beta_gdp * lag_gdp[i] +
             beta_unrate * lag_unrate[i] +
             beta_inflation * lag_inflation[i] +
             beta_ip * lag_ip[i] +
             beta_spread * lag_spread[i]

    y[i] ~ dt(mu[i], tau, nu)
  }

  # Priors for coefficients
  beta_0         ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  beta_gdp       ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  beta_unrate    ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  beta_inflation ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  beta_ip        ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  beta_spread    ~ dnorm(0, 1)

  # Prior for sigma
  sigma ~ dunif(0, 10)
  tau <- pow(sigma, -2)

  # Prior for degrees of freedom
  nu_minus_two ~ dexp(1/30)
  nu <- nu_minus_two + 2
}
"

# Pass data and hyperparameter values
y <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$gdp_growth)
lag_gdp <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_gdp_growth)
lag_unrate <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_unrate)
lag_inflation <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_inflation)
lag_ip <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_ip_growth)
lag_spread <- as.vector(df_final_scaled$lag_spread)

N <- length(y)

the_data_t <- list(
  y = y,
  lag_gdp = lag_gdp,
  lag_unrate = lag_unrate,
  lag_inflation = lag_inflation,
  lag_ip = lag_ip,
  lag_spread = lag_spread,
  N = N
)

initsfunction_t <- function(chain) {
  list(
    .RNG.seed = 200 + chain,
    .RNG.name = "base::Mersenne-Twister",
    sigma = 1,
    nu_minus_two = 10
  )
}

posterior_t <- run.jags(
  model = modelString_t,
  n.chains = 3,
  data = the_data_t,
  monitor = c("beta_0", "beta_gdp", "beta_unrate",
              "beta_inflation", "beta_ip", "beta_spread",
              "sigma", "nu"),
  adapt = 2000,
  burnin = 10000,
  sample = 10000,
  thin = 10,
  inits = initsfunction_t
)

summary(posterior_t)
```

```{r}
# Plot gianostic plots
plot(posterior_t, vars = c("beta_gdp", "beta_unrate", "beta_inflation",
                           "beta_ip", "beta_spread", "sigma", "nu"))
```

```{r}
# Convert posterior draws to matrix
post_t <- as.matrix(as.mcmc(posterior_t))

# Define vector of param names
t_params <- c("beta_0", "beta_gdp", "beta_unrate",
              "beta_inflation", "beta_ip", "beta_spread", "sigma", "nu")

# Compute mean, upper and lower bounds
t_mean  <- apply(post_t[, t_params], 2, mean)
t_lower <- apply(post_t[, t_params], 2, quantile, probs = 0.025)
t_upper <- apply(post_t[, t_params], 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)

# Create summary table
t_summary_table <- data.frame(
  Parameter = t_params,
  Mean = t_mean,
  CrI_2.5 = t_lower,
  CrI_97.5 = t_upper
)

# Display table
knitr::kable(
  t_summary_table,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Posterior summary for Bayesian regression with Student-t errors"
)
```

```{r}
# Design matrix for scaled predictors

  ~ lag_gdp_growth + lag_unrate + lag_inflation + lag_ip_growth + lag_spread,

)

# Combine coeffecient draws
beta_draws_t <- cbind(
  post_t[, "beta_0"],
  post_t[, "beta_gdp"],
  post_t[, "beta_unrate"],
  post_t[, "beta_inflation"],
  post_t[, "beta_ip"],
  post_t[, "beta_spread"]
)

# Compute mu and draw mean

```

```{r}
# Define model string for unscaled t model
modelString_t_unscaled <- "
model {

  for (i in 1:N) {
    mu[i] <- beta_0 +
             beta_gdp * lag_gdp[i] +
             beta_unrate * lag_unrate[i] +
             beta_inflation * lag_inflation[i] +
             beta_ip * lag_ip[i] +
             beta_spread * lag_spread[i]

    y[i] ~ dt(mu[i], tau, nu)
  }

  beta_0         ~ dnorm(0, 1/25)
  beta_gdp       ~ dnorm(0, 1/25)
  beta_unrate    ~ dnorm(0, 1/25)
  beta_inflation ~ dnorm(0, 1/25)
  beta_ip        ~ dnorm(0, 1/25)
  beta_spread    ~ dnorm(0, 1/25)

  sigma ~ dunif(0, 0.1)
  tau <- pow(sigma, -2)

  nu_minus_two ~ dexp(1/30)
  nu <- nu_minus_two + 2
}
"

# Pass data and hyperparameter values
y <- as.vector(df_final$gdp_growth)
lag_gdp <- as.vector(df_final$lag_gdp_growth)
lag_unrate <- as.vector(df_final$lag_unrate)
lag_inflation <- as.vector(df_final$lag_inflation)
lag_ip <- as.vector(df_final$lag_ip_growth)
lag_spread <- as.vector(df_final$lag_spread)

N <- length(y)

the_data_t_unscaled <- list(
  y = y,
  lag_gdp = lag_gdp,
  lag_unrate = lag_unrate,
  lag_inflation = lag_inflation,
  lag_ip = lag_ip,
  lag_spread = lag_spread,
  N = N
)

initsfunction_t_unscaled <- function(chain) {
  list(
    .RNG.seed = 200 + chain,
    .RNG.name = "base::Mersenne-Twister",
    sigma = 0.01,
    nu_minus_two = 10
  )
}

posterior_t_unscaled <- run.jags(
  model = modelString_t_unscaled,
  n.chains = 3,
  data = the_data_t_unscaled,
  monitor = c("beta_0", "beta_gdp", "beta_unrate",
              "beta_inflation", "beta_ip", "beta_spread",
              "sigma", "nu"),
  adapt = 2000,
  burnin = 10000,
  sample = 10000,
  thin = 10,
  inits = initsfunction_t_unscaled,
  method = "parallel"
)

# Give summary of draws
summary(posterior_t_unscaled)

# Convert results to matrix form
post_t_unscaled <- as.matrix(as.mcmc(posterior_t_unscaled))

# Create design matrix for unscaled data
X_unscaled <- model.matrix(
  ~ lag_gdp_growth + lag_unrate + lag_inflation + lag_ip_growth + lag_spread,
  data = df_final
)

# Combine coefficient draws
beta_draws_t_unscaled <- cbind(
  post_t_unscaled[, "beta_0"],
  post_t_unscaled[, "beta_gdp"],
  post_t_unscaled[, "beta_unrate"],
  post_t_unscaled[, "beta_inflation"],
  post_t_unscaled[, "beta_ip"],
  post_t_unscaled[, "beta_spread"]
)

# Compute and extract desired params
mu_draws_t <- beta_draws_t_unscaled %*% t(X_unscaled)
sigma_draws_t <- post_t_unscaled[, "sigma"]
nu_draws_t <- post_t_unscaled[, "nu"]

# PCompute posterior probability of negative GDP growth for each quarter
bayes_t_prob_neg <- sapply(1:ncol(mu_draws_t), function(j) {
  mean(pt((0 - mu_draws_t[, j]) / sigma_draws_t, df = nu_draws_t))
})

# Store results
df_final$bayes_t_prob_neg <- bayes_t_prob_neg
```
```{r}
# Plot diagnostic plots of simulation
plot(posterior_t_unscaled, vars = c("beta_gdp", "beta_unrate", "beta_inflation",
                           "beta_ip", "beta_spread", "sigma", "nu"))
```

## Reduced model

```{r}
# Define reduced model predictors via robust regression
reduced_vars <- c("lag_inflation", "lag_ip_growth")
```

```{r}
# Reduced formula on scaled data
reduced_formula <- as.formula(
  paste("gdp_growth ~", paste(reduced_vars, collapse = " + "))
)

# Fit reduced frequentist model on scaled data
freq_mod_reduced <- lm(reduced_formula, data = df_final_scaled)

# Display summary
summary(freq_mod_reduced)

# Robust SE results
robust_vcov_reduced <- vcovHC(freq_mod_reduced, type = "HC1")
robust_test_reduced <- coeftest(freq_mod_reduced, vcov = robust_vcov_reduced)

# Display results
robust_test_reduced
```

```{r}
# Store reduced regression metrics
freq_red_est <- robust_test_reduced[, "Estimate"]
freq_red_se  <- robust_test_reduced[, "Std. Error"]
freq_red_p   <- robust_test_reduced[, "Pr(>|t|)"]
freq_red_lo  <- freq_red_est - 1.96 * freq_red_se
freq_red_hi  <- freq_red_est + 1.96 * freq_red_se

# Create metrics table
freq_reduced_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(robust_test_reduced),
  Estimate = as.numeric(freq_red_est),
  Robust_SE = as.numeric(freq_red_se),
  CI_Lower = as.numeric(freq_red_lo),
  CI_Upper = as.numeric(freq_red_hi),
  P_Value = as.numeric(freq_red_p)
)

# Display table
knitr::kable(
  freq_reduced_table,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Reduced frequentist model with robust standard errors"
)
```

```{r}
# Fit reduced frequentist model on unscaled data
freq_mod_reduced_unscaled <- lm(reduced_formula, data = df_final)

# Display summary
summary(freq_mod_reduced_unscaled)

# Predict with model
pred_red <- predict(freq_mod_reduced_unscaled, newdata = df_final, se.fit = TRUE)

# Calculate desired values from predictions
mu_hat_red <- pred_red$fit
se_mu_red  <- pred_red$se.fit
sigma_hat_red <- sigma(freq_mod_reduced_unscaled)
pred_sd_red <- sqrt(se_mu_red^2 + sigma_hat_red^2)

# Probability of negative GDP growth
recession_prob_red <- pnorm(0, mean = mu_hat_red, sd = pred_sd_red)

# Store in dataframe
df_final$pred_gdp_growth_red <- mu_hat_red
df_final$pred_sd_red <- pred_sd_red
df_final$recession_prob_red <- recession_prob_red
```

```{r}
      col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, lty = 4)

lines(df_final$date, df_final$bayes_prob_neg_red,
      col = "purple", lwd = 2, lty = 5)

legend("topleft",
       legend = c(
         "Frequentist (Full)",
         "Bayesian Normal (Full)",
         "Bayesian t (Full)",
         "Frequentist (Reduced)",
         "Bayesian Normal (Reduced)"
       ),
       col = c("black", "red", "blue", "darkgreen", "purple"),
       lwd = 2,
       lty = c(1,2,3,4,5),
       bty = "n",
       cex = 0.6)
```
## Rolling Bayesian Model (shifting window)

```{r}
# Define constants for simulation
window_size <- 80
n_total <- nrow(df_final)
total_windows <- n_total - window_size + 1

# Initialize dataframe for results
rolling_results <- data.frame()

# Define progress bar
pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = total_windows, style = 3)

# Loop through all windows and perform JAGS simulation
for (start_idx in 1:total_windows) {

  # Track progress through bar
  setTxtProgressBar(pb, start_idx)
  cat(sprintf("  Window %d of %d\r", start_idx, total_windows))

  # Define end index
  end_idx <- start_idx + window_size - 1
  df_window <- df_final[start_idx:end_idx, ]

  # Extract windowed data for each predictor and response
  y_win <- as.vector(df_window$gdp_growth)
  lag_gdp_win <- as.vector(df_window$lag_gdp_growth)
  lag_unrate_win <- as.vector(df_window$lag_unrate)
  lag_inflation_win <- as.vector(df_window$lag_inflation)
  lag_ip_win <- as.vector(df_window$lag_ip_growth)
  lag_spread_win <- as.vector(df_window$lag_spread)

  the_data_win <- list(
    y = y_win,
    lag_gdp = lag_gdp_win,
    lag_unrate = lag_unrate_win,
    lag_inflation = lag_inflation_win,
    lag_ip = lag_ip_win,
    lag_spread = lag_spread_win,
    N = length(y_win),
    mu0 = 0, g0 = 1/25,
    mu1 = 0, g1 = 1/25,
    mu2 = 0, g2 = 1/25,
    mu3 = 0, g3 = 1/25,
    mu4 = 0, g4 = 1/25,
    mu5 = 0, g5 = 1/25,
    mu_sigma = 0,
    tau_sigma = 1/25,
    nu_sigma = 1,
    upper_sigma = 1e6
  )

  fit_win <- NULL

  # Try catch to remedy invalid model run
  tryCatch(
    {
      capture.output(
        fit_win <- run.jags(
          model = modelString,
          n.chains = 2,
          data = the_data_win,
          monitor = c("beta_gdp", "beta_unrate", "beta_inflation", "beta_ip", "beta_spread"),
          adapt = 1000,
          burnin = 3000,
          sample = 3000,
          thin = 5,
          inits = initsfunction,
          method = "rjags",
          summarise = TRUE
        ),
        file = NULL
      )
    },
    error = function(e) {
      message(sprintf("\nWindow %d failed: %s", start_idx, e$message))
    }
  )

  if (is.null(fit_win)) {
    next
  }

  # Store summary
  summ <- summary(fit_win)

  # Format results in dataframe
  rolling_results <- rbind(
    rolling_results,
    data.frame(
      end_date = df_window$date[nrow(df_window)],

      beta_gdp_mean = summ["beta_gdp", "Mean"],
      beta_gdp_low = summ["beta_gdp", "Lower95"],
      beta_gdp_high = summ["beta_gdp", "Upper95"],

      beta_unrate_mean = summ["beta_unrate", "Mean"],
      beta_unrate_low = summ["beta_unrate", "Lower95"],
      beta_unrate_high = summ["beta_unrate", "Upper95"],

      beta_inflation_mean = summ["beta_inflation", "Mean"],
      beta_inflation_low = summ["beta_inflation", "Lower95"],
      beta_inflation_high = summ["beta_inflation", "Upper95"],

      beta_ip_mean = summ["beta_ip", "Mean"],
      beta_ip_low = summ["beta_ip", "Lower95"],
      beta_ip_high = summ["beta_ip", "Upper95"],

      beta_spread_mean = summ["beta_spread", "Mean"],
      beta_spread_low = summ["beta_spread", "Lower95"],
      beta_spread_high = summ["beta_spread", "Upper95"]
    )
  )
}

close(pb)
cat("\nDone.\n")
```

# 7.) PPC

## Normal PPC
```{r}
# Posterior draws from normal Bayesian model
post_norm <- as.matrix(as.mcmc(posterior_MLR))

# Design matrix
X_unscaled <- model.matrix(
  ~ lag_gdp_growth + lag_unrate + lag_inflation + lag_ip_growth + lag_spread,
  data = df_final
)

# Coefficient draws
beta_draws_norm <- cbind(
  post_norm[, "beta_0"],
  post_norm[, "beta_gdp"],
  post_norm[, "beta_unrate"],
  post_norm[, "beta_inflation"],
  post_norm[, "beta_ip"],
  post_norm[, "beta_spread"]
)

# Posterior means for each observation
mu_post_norm <- beta_draws_norm %*% t(X_unscaled)
sigma_post_norm <- post_norm[, "sigma"]

# Simulate replicated datasets
set.seed(123)
n_draws <- nrow(mu_post_norm)

yrep_norm <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_draws, ncol = ncol(mu_post_norm))

for (s in 1:n_draws) {
  yrep_norm[s, ] <- rnorm(
    n = ncol(mu_post_norm),
    mean = mu_post_norm[s, ],
    sd = sigma_post_norm[s]
  )
}
```

## T Bayesian PPC
```{r}
# Define constants for PPC sim
set.seed(123)
n_draws_t <- nrow(mu_post_t)

# Posterior draws from t Bayesian model
post_t <- as.matrix(as.mcmc(posterior_t_unscaled))

# Combine draws
beta_draws_t <- cbind(
  post_t[, "beta_0"],
  post_t[, "beta_gdp"],
  post_t[, "beta_unrate"],
  post_t[, "beta_inflation"],
  post_t[, "beta_ip"],
  post_t[, "beta_spread"]
)

# Compute and extract desired params
mu_post_t <- beta_draws_t %*% t(X_unscaled)
sigma_post_t <- post_t[, "sigma"]
nu_post_t <- post_t[, "nu"]

# Initialize predicted value storage
yrep_t <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_draws_t, ncol = ncol(mu_post_t))

# Populate PPC data matrix
for (s in 1:n_draws_t) {
  yrep_t[s, ] <- mu_post_t[s, ] + sigma_post_t[s] * rt(ncol(mu_post_t), df = nu_post_t[s])
}
```

```{r}
# Observed data
y_obs <- df_final$gdp_growth

# Define function that combines PPC metrics into summaries
ppc_stats <- function(y) {
  c(
    mean = mean(y),
    sd = sd(y),
    min = min(y),
    prop_negative = mean(y < 0),
    n_extreme_neg = sum(y < -0.02)
  )
}

# Summary for observed vals
obs_stats <- ppc_stats(y_obs)

# Summary for replications from normal model
rep_stats_norm <- t(apply(yrep_norm, 1, ppc_stats))

# Summary for replicated from t model
rep_stats_t <- t(apply(yrep_t, 1, ppc_stats))
```

```{r}
# Create table
ppp_table <- data.frame(
  Statistic = names(obs_stats),
  Observed = as.numeric(obs_stats),
  PPP_Normal = sapply(1:length(obs_stats), function(j) mean(rep_stats_norm[, j] >= obs_stats[j])),
  PPP_t = sapply(1:length(obs_stats), function(j) mean(rep_stats_t[, j] >= obs_stats[j]))
)

# DIsplay table
knitr::kable(
  ppp_table,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Posterior predictive checks for Bayesian normal and Bayesian t models"
)
```

```{r}
# Threshold for extreme recession
extreme_cutoff <- -0.02

# Frequentist probability of extreme negative GDP
freq_extreme_prob <- pnorm(
  extreme_cutoff,
  mean = mu_hat,
  sd = pred_sd
)

# Bayesian t-model probability (you already have draws)
bayes_t_extreme_prob <- sapply(1:ncol(mu_draws_t), function(j) {
  mean(pt((extreme_cutoff - mu_draws_t[, j]) / sigma_draws_t, df = nu_draws_t))
})

# Plot comparison
plot(df_final$date, freq_extreme_prob,
     type = "l",
     lwd = 2,
     col = "black",
     ylim = range(c(freq_extreme_prob, bayes_t_extreme_prob), na.rm = TRUE),
     main = "Extreme Negative GDP Risk: Normal vs t-Model",
     xlab = "Quarter",
     ylab = "Probability (GDP < -2%)")

lines(df_final$date, bayes_t_extreme_prob,
      col = "red",
      lwd = 2,
      lty = 2)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("Frequentist (Normal)", "Bayesian t-model"),
       col = c("black", "red"),
       lwd = 2,
       lty = c(1, 2),
       bty = "n")
```

```{r}
############################################################
# Residual Distribution: Normal vs t Fit
############################################################

library(MASS)

# Residuals from frequentist model
residuals_freq <- resid(freq_mod_unscaled)
residuals_freq <- residuals_freq[is.finite(residuals_freq)]

# Normal fit
mu_norm <- mean(residuals_freq)
sd_norm <- sd(residuals_freq)

# t fit with warning suppression
t_fit <- suppressWarnings(
  fitdistr(
    residuals_freq,
    densfun = "t",
    start = list(
      m = median(residuals_freq),
      s = sd(residuals_freq),
      df = 4
    )
  )
)

# Extract t parameters
mu_t <- t_fit$estimate["m"]
sigma_t <- t_fit$estimate["s"]
nu_t <- t_fit$estimate["df"]

cat("t-distribution parameters:\n")
cat("mu =", mu_t, "\n")
cat("sigma =", sigma_t, "\n")
cat("nu (df) =", nu_t, "\n")

# Grid for density curves
x_grid <- seq(min(residuals_freq),
              max(residuals_freq),
              length.out = 500)

# Normal density
dens_norm <- dnorm(x_grid, mean = mu_norm, sd = sd_norm)

# t density
z_vals <- (x_grid - mu_t) / sigma_t
dens_t <- dt(z_vals, df = nu_t) / sigma_t
dens_t[!is.finite(dens_t)] <- 0

# Plot
hist(residuals_freq,
     breaks = 40,
     probability = TRUE,
     col = "lightgray",
     border = "white",
     main = "Residual Distribution: Normal vs t Fit",
     xlab = "Residuals")

lines(x_grid, dens_norm,
      col = "black",
      lwd = 2)

lines(x_grid, dens_t,
      col = "red",
      lwd = 2,
      lty = 2)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("Normal Fit", "t Fit"),
       col = c("black", "red"),
       lwd = 2,
       lty = c(1, 2),
       bty = "n")
```
